name: Encryption Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday encryption work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical encryption tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday encryption work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical encryption tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to encryption (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When encryption guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. State assumptions about encryption explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Keep encryption outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. When multiple encryption strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Check that encryption terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Document any non-obvious encryption decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Measure before optimizing any encryption bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
9. Prefer explicit, readable encryption solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Prefer the simplest encryption approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen encryption approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of encryption correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated encryption concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop encryption edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these encryption guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
